findings_verbatim.violated_requirement_or_invariant: REQ-027 / CONTROL-READY exact-owned-descendant cleanup safety: a force-kill must remain scoped to the recorded fixture descendant, including cleanup retries/finalizers.
findings_verbatim.concrete_trigger: After line 520 successfully taskkills the recorded descendant and lines 528-531 observe it absent, the operating system can reuse descendant_pid before the finally block at lines 550-554. _cleanup_pids then treats any process at that numeric PID as the fixture process and invokes taskkill /PID <pid> /T /F. The same PID-only finalizer is also used by the slow-success and lost-handle cases.
findings_verbatim.consequence: An unrelated process and its descendant tree can be force-terminated. A passing readback establishes only numeric-PID absence/presence, not that every force-kill was still owned by this fixture, so it cannot supply the claimed strict exact-owned-descendant cleanup proof.
findings_verbatim.smallest_owning_route: M03 only: strengthen control_child.py and test_fixture_controls.py to carry and verify a durable descendant identity (for example a nonce plus creation identity/validated command) immediately before each taskkill, and make a non-matching finalizer a safe no-op. Do not add an M02 production helper or change the frozen harness for this fixture-only repair.
